title: Staged rollback signal matrix and heuristics (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a staged rollback signal matrix and pragmatic heuristics. Meant to be a fast reference during releases where we want minimal user impact and clear automatic/manual handoffs. Not official docs — combine with infra runbooks and SRE on-call playbooks.

Context / assumptions:
- Applies to model or runtime releases that touch hosted API + dedicated pools.
- We have telemetry: per-route token counts, per-route latency histograms, 5xx/4xx rates, model confidence regression probes (eval-set score delta), and per-client error spikes.
- Default rolling window: 5m/15m/1h depending on signal.
- Goal: automatic soft-failover at low signal cost, escalate to manual 2nd-level for sustained/regressing metrics.

Signal categories (how I think about them):
1) Latency signals
   - baseline: 95th latency (p95) for route X (baseline from +7d median)
   - trigger (soft): p95 > baseline * 1.45 for 15m AND p50 > baseline * 1.3 -> initiate slow-drip rollback (reduce new cohort weight by 20%).
   - trigger (hard): p95 > baseline * 2.0 for 5m OR p99 spike > baseline * 3.0 -> immediate rollback to previous pinned version and page SRE.
   - notes: be careful with warmup effects if new model has longer init; add a 10m grace period for cold-start warmups.

2) Error / availability signals
   - soft: route 5xx rate increase > 0.3 percentage points absolute AND relative increase > 2x baseline over 10m -> cut traffic by 25% to new variant, start verbose tracing.
   - hard: absolute 5xx rate > 1.0% for 5m OR client-visible errors (user-reported) correlated with error logs -> full rollback and incident.
   - include circuit-breaker on downstream dependency timeouts: if dependent service timeout rate > 10% -> auto fallback to model-variant that bypasses that code path.

3) Quality (regression) signals
   - synthetic eval probes: daily eval set score delta <= -3% (absolute) over baseline -> quarantine rollout and reduce traffic to 0% for cohort after next checkpoint.
   - user-sentiment heuristics: spike in negative feedback tags > +30% vs baseline in 1h -> manual review (can't auto-rollback reliably without false positives).

4) Cost and throughput signals
   - token-per-request increase > 50% without corresponding latency drop/quality improvement -> auto-scale but flag for review (possible hallucination loop).

Action matrix (staged):
- Stage 0 (dry-run, 0% traffic): smoke tests only, no user traffic.
- Stage 1 (warmup cohort 1%, 5 min soak): check logs, p50/p95, trace samples. Manual ok threshold: any 5xx -> abort to stage 0.
- Stage 2 (drip to 5% over 20m): if soft signals -> hold and contact SE/PM. If hard signals -> immediate rollback.
- Stage 3 (anchor cohorts 20%): add health-check endpoints for observational reroutes. If soft signals here, decant in 10% slices every 10m.
- Stage 4 (wide 100%): final step; any hard signal -> global rollback with pre-baked fallback variant.

Automatic rollback steps (what the automation should do):
1) Mark deployment as "degraded" with reason tag (latency/error/quality).
2) Shift weights away from new variant according to policy (first 25%, then 50%, then 100%).
3) If pinned fallback exists, pin immediately and record who was auto-notified.
4) Create a debug trace bundle and attach to the incident for triage.

Manual escalation checklist (if automation escalates or human decides):
- Confirm metrics and correlate with client buckets (are all clients impacted or a cohort?).
- Pull top 5 traces and top 10 error logs for last 15m.
- Check infra autoscaler anomalies: GPU queuing, OOM, batch size bumps.
- Repro steps: curl a few representative routes with headers from affected clients (include token usage).
- If rollback: create a PR to pin previous image/version and push to canary config (note: keep PR fast, tagging required: release-hotfix/YYYYMMDD).

Pinning notes (how I personally do quick pins):
- For hosted: update deployment config (deployments/{route}/versions.json) -> set pinned_version = "vX.Y.Z" and push via infra-controlled CI job that updates runtime config.
- For dedicated pools: update pool manifest and, if needed, drain new nodes (scale down new variant groups).
- Communicate pin in #releases and add comment to INF-3421 with timestamp and reason.

Warmup cohort design (lessons):
- Avoid sending high-compute clients (large context) in first 5% cohort. Prefer low token clients to validate correctness first.
- Gradually increase max_tokens cap for cohorts 1->3.
- Force short inference windows to exercise KV cache heat-up without heavy tail cost.

Practical commands / snippets I keep handy:
- Check recent error rate (kusto-like pseudocmd):
  metrics.query("route=routeX AND metric=5xx | summarize rate by 5m")
- Quick rollback curl (example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/rollout -d '{"route":"routeX","action":"pin","version":"v1.2.7"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'

Open questions / TODOs (for me or followups):
- Do we have a canonical signal store query that combines user-reported incidents + telemetry? I think INF-3421 started this work but not finished. (ask Marco)
- SRE runbook: need explicit decision tree for when dependency latency vs model latency attributions conflict.
- Should we add model-confidence based automatic throttles for hallucination-sensitive routes? Drafting a simple heuristic: if avg_confidence_drop > 0.12 AND user_feedback_spike then auto-hold.
- Add a small code change to deployment agent to support "graceful drain -> pin" atomic operation (right now it's two steps).

Quick log of last two incidents (memory for postmortem):
- 2025-08-02: rollout v2.8.0 -> p95 increased 1.6x due to kernel change; automation cut to 40% but never reached full rollback because drain policy hung; manual rollback after 40m. Root cause: grpc connection pooling bug.
- 2025-11-18: model variant A introduced token inflation on long prompts; increased cost by 2.5x for a subset of clients. We did targeted pin for top-10 spenders and staged-wide rollback. Took ~3h to clean billing spikes.

Notes-to-self for next release:
- Add a small smoke-eval harness that runs 25 short prompts and computes answer-sanity; put it in stage 1.
- Coordinate with billing to have a rapid temporary quota adjustment for clients affected by token inflation.
- Rehearse the "pin previous version" flow in next dry-run session.

Bottom line: keep the automation conservative and the human handover really clear. Favor quick pins to known-good versions over long investigations that keep degraded variant live.

End of scratchpad.
